<meta>continues from previous page. This passage is from the "Mountain Tree" chapter of the Zhuangzi. The marginal notes are the editor's commentary placed beside the lines they explain.</meta>

<margin>This is the conduct of the perfect man, who does not seek fame or advancement. So why, sir, do you take delight in being known?</margin>
...nor do others find fault with him. The perfect man is not heard of; why then do you delight in fame?" Confucius said, "Excellent!" He took leave of
<margin>He does not value finery.</margin>
his friends and acquaintances, dismissed his disciples, and fled into a great marsh. He wore furs and coarse cloth and ate acorns and chestnuts.
<margin>He does not prize fine food.</margin>
<margin>He does not stir up a mind that makes distinctions, and so does not disturb the flocks of birds and herds of beasts.</margin>
He walked among the beasts without disturbing their herds, and among the birds without disturbing their flights. Birds and beasts did not shun him; how much less would
<margin>Even creatures of another kind do not shun him.</margin>
<margin>Surname and given name of a recluse.</margin>
men! Confucius asked <term>Zisang Hu</term> <gloss>a recluse</gloss>: "Twice I have been driven out of Lu. In Song they felled a tree on me; in Wei they wiped out my tracks; I was reduced to hardship in Shang and Zhou; I was besieged between Chen and Cai. Since I have met with these several calamities, my close friends have grown ever more distant and my disciples and companions ever more scattered. Why is this?" Zisang Hu

<note>A small printer's mark or seal appears in the top right corner of the page.</note>

<summary>This page from the "Mountain Tree" chapter of the Zhuangzi tells how Confucius, rebuked for seeking renown, retires into a marsh and lives so simply that birds and beasts accept him; he then asks the recluse Zisang Hu why his misfortunes have driven his friends and disciples away. Marginal commentary explains the lines as the conduct of the perfect man who seeks no fame and makes no distinctions.</summary>
<keywords>Zhuangzi, Mountain Tree chapter, Confucius, Zisang Hu, recluse, perfect man, fame, simplicity, Lu, Song, Wei, Chen and Cai, Daoism, commentary</keywords>
